title: “Lord, help me notice my heart early—and choose humility before harm.”
paragraphs: “Lord, help me notice my heart early—and choose humility before harm.”
When I read the Bible, I often imagine standing nearby, watching quietly.
I stay hidden—barely breathing—watching jealousy take shape before it speaks or acts. Cain’s silence feels louder than words. Nothing has happened yet… and yet everything has.

I’m reminded how unchecked emotions grow in the quiet places of the heart.
I pause here.
What do I do with jealousy when it first stirs within me?

(Reflective pause…)
God speaks before the fall—but will Cain listen?
And will I?
💭 Share what this moment stirs in you
What small signs of jealousy do I notice in myself before they grow?
How does God’s warning to Cain speak into my own inner conflicts?
Am I more likely to hide my emotions—or bring them honestly before God?
What would it look like to respond differently at the very beginning?
